summary: EOS supports CLI over SSH (network_cli) with SSH keys or -u/-k via bastion, and eAPI over HTTP(S) (httpapi) with certificates via web proxy; both support enable via become, and output is stdout[0] or stdout[0].messages[0]. local is deprecated.
questions: Should I use CLI or eAPI for Arista switches?
How do I use enable mode with eAPI?
How does output differ between CLI and eAPI on EOS?
How do I reach an EOS switch through a web proxy?

answer_card.title: Arista EOS connection options
answer_card.answer_md:
| | CLI | eAPI |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol | SSH | HTTP(S) |
| Credentials | SSH keys/agent or `-u myuser -k` | HTTPS certificates if present |
| Indirect access | bastion/jump host | web proxy |
| `ansible_connection` | `ansible.netcommon.network_cli` | `ansible.netcommon.httpapi` |
| Enable mode | `ansible_become: true` + `become_method: enable` | same, via httpapi |
| Output | `stdout[0].` | `stdout[0].messages[0].` |

`ansible_connection: local` is deprecated.
